prompt:
You describe a timing diagram from an electronics datasheet for an engineer who cannot see it.

Cover, in this order:
1. Every signal, from top to bottom.
2. The sequence of edges and states in time order, and which edge triggers which.
3. Every named interval (for example tSU, tH) with its value and unit, if shown.

Figure type: timing diagram
Section: 19 Radio Control > 19.1 Power-On Start-Up Sequence > 19.1.1 Automatic POR
Caption: Figure 26: Power-On Reset
Text inside the figure (exact, from the PDF text layer): XOSC Stable CSn | SO
Text that mentions the figure: When the CC1101 reset is completed, the chip will be in the IDLE state and the crystal oscillator will be running. If the chip has had sufficient time for the crystal oscillator to stabilize after the power-on-reset, the SO pin will go low immediately after taking CSn low. If CSn is taken low before reset is completed, the SO pin will first go high, indicating that the crystal oscillator is not stabilized, before going low as shown in Figure 26.

Rules:
- When a name or number from "Text inside the figure" is visible in the image, copy it exactly, character for character.
- Never invent a value, name, pin, unit or connection. If something is too small or blurry to read, write "unreadable" instead of guessing.
- Describe only what this image shows. Do not explain general theory or add advice.
- Mention each item once. Stop when everything is covered.
- Plain text only: no Markdown headings, tables or bold. Short paragraphs and "- " lists are fine.
- Start directly with what the figure is (for example "Block diagram of ..."), not with "The image shows".

answer.text:
Timing diagram of Figure 26: Power-On Reset.

Signals from top to bottom:
CSn
SO

Sequence of edges and states in time order:
CSn starts high and transitions low.
SO starts high and transitions low after CSn goes low, provided the XOSC is stable.
If CSn is taken low before reset is completed, SO first goes high before going low.
The state XOSC Stable is indicated by an arrow pointing to the SO signal.

Named intervals:
No named intervals with values and units are shown.
